 Who is Joe Scally? published at 20:15 BST 20:15 BST 
 Stuttgart 1-1 Borussia M'gladbach 
 Joe Scally is an American fullback who has scored three of Borussia Monchengladbach’s nine goals this season. 
 The USA international has been with Monchengladbach since
2019 despite only being 23 years of age. He’s made over a 150 appearances for
Die Fohlen (The Foals) over the last seven years and is a crucial part of
Alexander Blessin’s side.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Stuttgart 1-0 Borussia M'gladbach

 The opening goal comes from a good strike from Ermedin Demirovic, but Moritz Nicolas in the Monchengladbach goal will not want to see this again.

 The goalkeeper should have done better but Stuttgart will not care one bit.

 'Well prepared and with full power' published at 19:28 BST 19:28 BST 
 Stuttgart v Borussia M'gladbach (19:30 GMT) 
 German Bundesliga 
 Image source, Getty Images Stuttgart manager Sebastian Hoeness said in a press conference in the build up to tonight's action: " “We’re going into the meeting with Borussia Mönchengladbach well prepared and with full power, and want to deliver the best performance we can with the support of our fans tomorrow night."
 On playing at home: “We’re looking forward to the second game under the lights in the space of four days, and what will certainly be another brilliant atmosphere at the MHP Arena.”

 Introducing the teams: Borussia Monchengladbach published at 19:26 BST 19:26 BST 
 Stuttgart v Borussia M'gladbach (19:30 GMT) 
 If
you thought Stuttgart had made a poor start to the season Borussia
Monchengladbach have got news for you.
 Die
Borussen have taken a grand total of zero points from the opening six games
meaning that they’ve made one of the poorest starts to a Bundesliga season in
recent memory.
 The
start was so poor that Eugen Polanski was dismissed after the first four
matches of the season.
 He
was replaced by ex-St Pauli manager Alexander Blessin who has yet failed to
arrest the slide, losing his first two matches in charge.
 Gladbach
have form for starting a season in poor fashion but turning it around in
spectacular fashion.
 Ten years ago Gladbach sat bottom of the league winless
after five matches before eventually finishing in fourth place in the
Bundesliga and qualifying for the Champions League.

 Stuttgart flying in Europe published at 19:24 BST 19:24 BST 
 Stuttgart v Borussia M'gladbach (19:30 GMT) 
 As mentioned Stuttgart won their opening two games of the Champions League league phrase competition, and dominated in the opening 45 minutes of their last game against Atletico Madrid but had to settle for a draw.
 The German side did not take the lead until the 36th minute, when Jamie Leweling scored from the edge of the area with a fine low strike to give the Bundesliga side a deserved advantage at the break.
 But they were made to rue their missed first-half chances when Argentina striker Julian Alvarez levelled the game just over a minute after the restart.
 Atletico looked like they might take control of the game but then Atletico midfielder Morten Hjulmand's challenge left them with 10 men for the final 26 minutes.
 That saw Stuttgart put them under pressure but they could not find a winner as defender Jeff Chabot headed wide their best opportunity from Maximilian Mittelstadt's corner.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Introducing the teams: Stuttgart published at 19:23 BST 19:23 BST 
 Stuttgart v Borussia M'gladbach (19:30 GMT) 
 Let's start with the home side shall we.
 Stuttgart’s league form is in
stark contrast to their form in Europe. 
 Where VFB are un-beaten with two wins
and a draw from their opening matches in the Champions League they’ve only
tasted victory twice in the Bundesliga against Cologne and Paderborn.
 The
four other matches have seen them suffer defeats with an opening day defeat
against Bayern Munich saw them concede five goals.
 Head
coach Sebastian Hoeness has been in charge of Die Schwaben (The Swabians) for
three and a half years now and brought with him success in the form of a
second-place finish in the 2023/24 Bundesliga a fourth placed finish in last
year’s Bundesliga that saw them return to the Champions League in between that
was a German Cup win giving Stuttgart their first trophy since the 2006/07
Bundesliga title.

 Welcome! Hi! published at 19:20 BST 19:20 BST 
 Stuttgart v Borussia M'gladbach (19:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Good evening! After a busy week of Champions League games, it's time for another Friday night of Bundesliga action.
 The
action gets underway on Friday night as this year’s Champions League surprise
package Stuttgart host Borussia Monchengladbach in their 109 meeting in the German top flight and you can watch it live on
BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport.
 Stuttgart
may have made a strong start to their Champions League campaign. They currently
sit in third place in Europe’s premier competition just behind PSG and
Liverpool with seven points coming from their opening three matches.
 Away
from Europe and it’s been a different story as Die Roten sit in 13th
place.
 Alongside Friday night’s live match, you’ll be able to watch highlights from all the weekend’s Bundesliga action on the BBC iPlayer on Sunday evening from 20:30 GMT.
